label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/insecure-randomness) is TP: Random.nextLong() at L72 flows to rememberMeKey at L102, which is used for session token generation - using non-cryptographic Random for auth tokens is a recognized weakness. Alert 2 (java/xss) is FP: The sink at L111-L116 writes rememberMe.getName() and rememberMe.getValue() which derive from server-side constructed cookieName (from class name) and rememberMeKey (from Random), neither being user-provided. User input from cookies is stored in param but reassigned to constant "This_should_always_happen" before reaching the sink.

evidence.note: Random.nextLong() generates rememberMeKey used for session tokens
Sink prints server-derived cookieName and Random-based rememberMeKey, not user input
